candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the className and message strings written into an OpenWire command. Unmarshalling of ExceptionResponse.exception, ConnectionError.exception, MessageAck.poisonCause (and recursively the cause chain) reaches tightUnmarsalThrowable/looseUnmarsalThrowable, which pass the wire-supplied strings unmodified to createThrowable() -> Class.forName(className, ...) -> clazz.getConstructor(String.class) -> newInstance(message). No credentials, broker identity or prior authorization are needed to have the transport unmarshal a command.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the class name is wire-controlled and not derived from a fixed table (tightUnmarsalThrowable reads it with tightUnmarshalString, line 191). Checked that there is no allowlist or Throwable-assignability check before construction: no 'TrustedPackages' or allowlist symbol exists anywhere in the snapshot (search returned no match), and ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream (the untrusted-deserialization helper) is not used by this path. Checked the cast ordering: line 232 constructs the object before line 232's cast to Throwable, so the 'it is cast to Throwable' assumption does not constrain which class is instantiated. Checked the catch(Throwable) at line 233, which converts any failure into a benign Throwable rather than rejecting the packet. Checked that Class.forName is called with initialize=false, which only avoids static initializers, not constructor execution. Checked the default deployment: assembly/src/release/conf/activemq.xml lines 111-118 expose OpenWire on 0.0.0.0:61616 and define no authentication plugin, so the vulnerable unmarshalling runs before broker authentication. Checked that the affected helper is duplicated in the legacy module (v2-v8) and in v9/v10, i.e. the flaw is not confined to one protocol version. Not verified at runtime.
candidates.impact: Pre-authentication arbitrary class instantiation driven by unauthenticated network input on the broker's default OpenWire port. With a suitable class on the classpath (e.g. Spring context/XML-driven classes present in the standard distribution) this yields remote code execution in the broker JVM under the broker's OS account; otherwise it enables attacker-directed class loading and side-effecting constructors, plus possible availability impact, with failures silently swallowed.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Network reachability to an OpenWire listener; the stock distribution enables tcp://0.0.0.0:61616 and the default server config defines no authentication plugin, so commands are unmarshalled before broker-level authentication (addConnection). 2) For full code execution, a class with a public single-String-constructor that performs a dangerous action must be on the broker classpath; Spring's org.springframework.context.support.ClassPathXmlApplicationContext(String) is the canonical example and spring artifacts are part of the standard 5.x distribution (activemq-spring / conf/activemq.xml imported via Spring). Without such a class the flaw still permits attacker-selected class loading/instantiation with attacker-supplied constructor argument.
candidates.root_cause: BaseDataStreamMarshaller.createThrowable() takes a class name and a message string read directly from the wire (tightUnmarsalThrowable/looseUnmarsalThrowable) and performs Class.forName(className, false, loader) followed by clazz.getConstructor(String.class).newInstance(message). There is no allowlist, no package/type restriction and no check that the class is a Throwable before construction: the (Throwable) cast at line 232 happens only after the attacker-selected constructor has already run. Failures are swallowed by catch (Throwable e), which returns a generic Throwable, so a non-Throwable gadget class is instantiated silently. The same unguarded helper is replicated across every OpenWire version shipped in this snapshot (client v1/v9/v10 and legacy v2-v8).
candidates.title: Pre-auth arbitrary class instantiation via attacker-controlled class name in OpenWire throwable unmarshalling
candidates.trace: Remote TCP bytes -> OpenWireFormat.unmarshal -> generated *Marshaller.tightUnmarshal (e.g. ExceptionResponseMarshaller line 69, MessageAckMarshaller line 76, ConnectionErrorMarshaller line 69) -> BaseDataStreamMarshaller.tightUnmarsalThrowable (v1 lines 188-226 / v10 lines 187-225): reads className and message from the DataInput -> createThrowable(clazz, message) (v1 lines 228-236 / v10 lines 227-236) -> Class.forName(className, false, ...) line 230 -> clazz.getConstructor(new Class[]{String.class}) line 231 -> constructor.newInstance(new Object[]{message}) line 232. The constructor body of the attacker-chosen class executes at line 232; the (Throwable) cast and any type check occur only afterwards, and any resulting Throwable (including ClassCastException) is caught at line 233 and replaced with a generic Throwable, hiding the attempt.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no payload was crafted. The availability of a specific gadget class (e.g. Spring ClassPathXmlApplicationContext) in a given deployment's classpath was inferred from module dependencies and distribution configuration, not executed. The exact broker-side command-dispatch path after unmarshalling (transport vs. broker service) and OpenWire protocol-version negotiation were traced by source reading only, not runtime-verified. Exploitability therefore depends on both network exposure of the OpenWire connector and the classpath of the target JVM.
candidates.weakness_type: Externally controlled class instantiation / unsafe reflection on untrusted deserialized data (deserialization-class flaw)

coverage_summary: Read-only source review of the assigned ActiveMQ 5.11.0 snapshot: 2446 source files in scope (per get_source_scope; binaries skipped, no symlinks, no sensitive-name exclusions), 2055 Java files parsed by the P1 relation index (2378 files indexed, 68 source files not indexed, 71 omitted files; index reports no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution and no runtime reachability). All test sources are absent from the snapshot (e.g. activemq-client/src/test is empty, activemq-unit-tests contains only pom.xml/.gitignore), so no test-based evidence was available. Areas examined in source: OpenWire marshalling (client v1/v9/v10 and legacy v2-v8, including throwable unmarshalling callers in ExceptionResponse/ConnectionError/MessageAck marshallers), broker security/authorization (SimpleAuthenticationBroker, AuthorizationBroker, JAAS/LDAP maps), the fileserver webapp (RestFilter, IOHelper, FilenameGuardFilter, web.xml, jetty.xml), web/REST servlets and web-console configuration, console tooling, blob message handling, and KahaDB/levelDB deserialization paths. Index facts were used only for navigation; all candidate paths and the selected tracing were re-verified against source text. No code, tests, scanners or payloads were executed.
limitations: No execution, build, test or runtime verification was performed; all conclusions are static and source-based.

The P1 index has no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution, 68 source files are missing from it, and 71 files were omitted; code areas without index records were not reviewed merely because they are absent from the index.
Test sources are stripped from the snapshot, so exploitability or regression evidence from tests could not be used.

The OpenWire finding's RCE impact depends on a suitable class (gadget) being present on the target classpath and on the deployment exposing the OpenWire connector; classpath composition was inferred from module/POM and distribution configuration, not verified by running the broker.

Whether the stock 5.11.0 binary distribution bundles spring-context (needed for the ClassPathXmlApplicationContext-class gadget) was inferred from the project's Spring-based configuration and activemq-spring module rather than from a resolved dependency tree.
The fileserver lead's exposure depends on the deployment importing jetty.xml; the default assembly does import it, but a minimal broker configuration would not expose HTTP at all.
Non-Java artifacts (JSPs, JavaScript, XML descriptors) were only sampled, not exhaustively reviewed.

rejected_leads.lead: activemq-fileserver RestFilter (activemq-fileserver/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/util/RestFilter.java lines 103-189) performs HTTP PUT/MOVE/DELETE with no authentication unless the optional 'write-permission-role' init-parameter is configured; the shipped web.xml (activemq-fileserver/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml lines 26-44) sets no such init-parameter, and assembly/src/release/conf/jetty.xml (lines 40-47, 68-73) applies no security constraint to /fileserver while deploying that webapp by default at http://0.0.0.0:8161/fileserver. doMove (lines 113-124) parses the attacker-supplied 'Destination' header with new URL(...) and copies the request file to new File(url.getFile()), i.e. an arbitrary absolute filesystem path -> unauthenticated arbitrary file write as the broker user (path to code execution via dropped webapp/config/authorized_keys content). Not submitted only because of the one-candidate cap; ranked just below the OpenWire issue because it is partly a missing-default-authorization/feature-design issue and requires the web console deployment (default in the binary distribution but disabled if jetty.xml is not imported).
rejected_leads.reason: Ranked second; unsubmitted due to the single-candidate limit, not because the source evidence is weak.

rejected_leads.lead: ActiveMQObjectMessage.getObject() (activemq-client/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/command/ActiveMQObjectMessage.java lines 180-202) deserializes message content with ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream (activemq-client/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/util/ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream.java lines 41-96), which resolves any class name from the stream via Class.forName with no allowlist or trusted-package filtering anywhere in the snapshot. A producer able to place an ObjectMessage on a queue/topic can therefore attack any consumer that calls getObject() (standard ObjectMessage deserialization RCE).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible but requires a downstream consumer/application to unmarshal the object, i.e. a weaker default-reachability story than the submitted pre-auth OpenWire issue.

rejected_leads.lead: KahaDB/ObjectMarshaller and message-database readObject paths (e.g. activemq-kahadb-store/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/store/kahadb/disk/util/ObjectMarshaller.java lines 47-51, MessageDatabase.java lines 686-712 and 3155-3159) deserialize local journal/metadata files without filtering.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires attacker write access to the broker's data directory (itself a post-compromise condition); not a primary remote vector.

rejected_leads.lead: Web console / REST layer input handling (activemq-web MessageServlet/MessageListenerServlet, QueueBrowseServlet rendering user-supplied selector/message content) looked like possible reflected/stored XSS or selector injection.
rejected_leads.reason: No concrete unescaped sink with attacker-controlled data and security impact was confirmed within the time budget; left unconfirmed.

summary: Review of the Apache ActiveMQ 5.11.0 source snapshot (2446 files, 2055 parsed Java files; no test sources are present in the snapshot). Broad pass over the wire-format/unmarshalling code, broker security plugins (simple/JAAS/Shiro authorization), the fileserver webapp, the web/REST console layer, console tooling, KahaDB/leveldb (de)serialization, and blob handling. One candidate is submitted: pre-authentication, attacker-controlled class instantiation in the OpenWire throwable unmarshalling path (BaseDataStreamMarshaller.createThrowable), which is reachable from bytes sent to the default tcp://0.0.0.0:61616 connector with no authentication plugin configured. Two other plausible issues (fileserver REST arbitrary file write; ObjectMessage deserialization with no allowlist) are recorded as unsubmitted leads because only one candidate may be filed.
